audit_findings.title: Known 2026 capital spending may be missing while the funding cash is added to equity value
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $320 million FY2026 expected capital expenditures; filed $120 million spent in H1 2026; computed approximately $200 million remaining
audit_findings.mechanism: A capital outflow omitted from forecast owner earnings while the associated funding cash is added in the equity bridge double-counts cash available to owners.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures in 2026 are expected to be approximately $400 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q supersedes the earlier $400 million estimate with $320 million and shows that $120 million was already spent before the $228 million bridge cash date. The $90.1 million anchor also approximates 2025 operating cash flow of $382 million less $291 million of capital expenditures, so complete omission is not demonstrated. Nevertheless, if the approximately $200 million remaining program is neither borne by forecast owner earnings nor reserved from bridge cash, the overstatement could approach $2.81 per share before considering discounting or benefits from expansion—about 12% to 17% of the stated scenario values. That is materially capable of changing the modeled value, although it would not close the gap to the $68.17 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile forecast-year owner earnings line by line to the updated $320 million program, identify maintenance versus expansion capital, confirm how the $120 million already spent is reflected, and rerun all scenarios after reserving any unfunded remaining outlay from the $228 million bridge cash.

audit_findings.title: Temporary cash-tax deferral may have been capitalized as recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporarily reduced cash taxes increase the FY2025 owner-earnings anchor; growing that anchor capitalizes the benefit unless later tax payments are modeled.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain provisions of The Tax Act decreased cash taxes paid during the year and may change the timing of cash tax payments in future periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a timing benefit but does not quantify the portion attributable to the Tax Act or its reversal schedule. FY2025 tax expense was $50 million versus $42 million of cash taxes paid, while the deferred-tax provision was $24 million and net deferred-tax liabilities increased by $28 million. Those figures show timing differences but do not isolate the owner-earnings overstatement. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $50 million tax provision to the $42 million cash payment by provision, isolate bonus-depreciation and research-expensing deferrals, obtain the expected reversal schedule, and rerun the valuation with normalized cash taxes and explicit reversals.

audit_findings.title: Foreign-exchange losses may be recurring economic costs despite cash-flow add-backs
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $11 million 2025 cash-flow add-back and $15 million 2025 P&L foreign-currency loss
audit_findings.mechanism: Using operating cash flow in owner earnings adds back current noncash remeasurement and transaction losses; value is overstated if recurring operating exposures later require cash settlement and are not otherwise normalized.
audit_findings.evidence: We historically have not entered into currency rate hedges with respect to our exposure from operations, although we may do so in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: The $11 million add-back equals 12.2% of the $90.1 million anchor and is therefore potentially meaningful, but treating all of it as a recurring cash cost is not supported. Reported FX results also changed from a $40 million loss in 2023 to a $9 million gain in 2024, a $15 million loss in 2025, and a $4 million gain in H1 2026. The record does not separate translation, remeasurement, intercompany balances, and settled operating transactions, so the sustainable value effect remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 $11 million cash-flow add-back and $15 million P&L loss by currency and balance, identify subsequent settlements, exclude pure translation effects, calculate a normalized recurring cash FX cost, and rerun the owner-earnings anchor if nonzero.

audit_findings.title: Environmental contingencies are senior cash claims whose ultimate amount is uncapped by the recorded reserve
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $27 million reserve, including $1 million current; excess exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Environmental settlements reduce future owner cash flow or excess cash in the equity bridge, particularly where prior accrual expense is excluded from current-period owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: While no estimate of the range of any such change can be made at this time, the amount that we may ultimately pay in connection with these matters could materially exceed, in either the near term or the longer term, the amounts accrued to date.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing confirms a $27 million undiscounted reserve and warns that ultimate payments could materially exceed it, but provides no estimable range for the excess. Deducting the recorded reserve alone would reduce value by approximately $0.38 per share, only about 1.6% to 2.3% of stated scenario equity values; that known amount is not material by itself. The unreserved exposure could be material, but its amount and timing cannot be established, so the broader finding remains open and uncertain rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the site-level reserve and payment schedule, identify insurance and third-party recoveries, test whether forecast owner earnings include reserve runoff, and rerun the bridge for the $27 million recorded claim plus separately disclosed low, base, and high remediation estimates when supportable.
